Elliot — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a small set of asks so we can put a concise economics package together for Helix: 

1) Confirmed/assumed volumes (what you stated on the call):
   - Initial steady state: ~400M tokens / month
   - Growth plan: ~25% Q-over-Q in year 1 (we'll size for first 6 months, then plan cadence)

2) Environments you want covered: prod, staging, dev (3 environments total).

3) Primary commercial asks from your side:
   - Target unit economics (ballpark $/1M tokens) you were comfortable with for a private deployment
   - Preferred licensing model: per-environment flat license vs. per-GPU pool commit
   - Support expectations (SLA/response, optional block-hours for integrations)

Next steps we propose:
 - Rishi will sketch a unit-econ model with two commitment tiers (12m commit, and 36m deeper discount) and show how license + infra maps to $/1M tokens.
 - We'll attach a short econ worksheet and a one-page terms summary for you to share with procurement.
 - Can you confirm procurement contact (cc'd or direct email) and whether Helix requires SOC2 + HSM/KMS for onboarding?

If the above looks right I'll ask Rishi + Marissa to add details and send a formal Econ worksheet by EOD.

Thanks,
Grace

Thanks Grace — that matches the call. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Volumes: initial pilot is actually 300-450M tokens/month (varies by feature). Use 400M as a working number.
- Envs: yes — 3 environments. Production must meet 99.9% availability (internal SLAs).
- Budget: procurement gave a high-level range for year 1 of $60k — $140k (includes license + infra run costs). They asked for a target $/1M tokens number to test vs. their internal benchmarks: they'd like to see options centered around $5–$8 / 1M tokens (we said private may be higher than hosted; they understand).
- Licensing preference: they prefer a predictable environment-based license (capex-style) rather than purely per-GPU consumption, but will consider a mixed model if it lowers unit costs.
- Security: SOC 2 required; KMS/HSM is preferred but not mandatory for pilot. Procurement contact is procurement@helixhealth.com (Procurement Lead: Ana Velez).

Can you include both a per-environment license option and a per-GPU commit option in the worksheet so we can present both to procurement? Also flag any material one-time onboarding fees (security review / network validation) in the term summary.

Best,
Elliot
Product Lead, Caret Solutions (working with Helix)

Elliot — thanks for the clarification. I've sketched two parallel price frameworks and attached a simple econ worksheet: HLX-econ-model-20270322.xlsx and a one-page term summary. High level: 

A) Per-environment license (preferred by Helix) — predictable model
   - License fee: $18,000 / environment / year (covers runtime, control plane, basic observability)
   - Support (standard): included; Premium support (SLA 99.9%, 4-hour P1 response + 24/7 coverage) = +$12,000 / year / account
   - Onboarding/security validation one-time professional services fee: $18,000 (covers SOC2 evidence handoff, KMS integration, network validation)

B) Committed GPU pool + token units (consumption hybrid) — lower unit $ if commit is large
   - Committed GPU pool price (example sizing for 400M tokens monthly sustained): equivalent to 2 x A100-80GB reserved throughput = $TBD (we show $45k/mo as a sample committed infra number in worksheet)
   - Unit token price after commit: $4.50 / 1M tokens (with 12-month commit tier)
   - Without commit (on-demand private), sticker token price: $9.00 / 1M tokens (higher variability)

Notes / translation to your $/1M ask:
 - If Helix picks per-environment license + premium support + onboarding, expected run-rate (license + support amortized + token cost on top) corresponds roughly to $6.5–$8 / 1M tokens in year 1 at 400M tokens/mo (we show the math in the worksheet).
 - If Helix chooses committed GPU pool + 12m commit, we can get to ~$4.5 / 1M tokens (our target for a mid-size enterprise commit).

Sizing and environment multiplier: keep in mind each additional environment increases base license linearly; however, caching and prefix reuse across environments can reduce effective token counts by ~10–15% in practice (we model this conservatively at 5%).

Attachments included: HLX-econ-model-20270322.xlsx (tabbed worksheet: "assumptions", "license_vs_commit", "sensitivity"), private-deploy-term-summary-20270322.pdf (one-pager).

Asks for procurement:
 - Confirm whether Helix prefers environment-based license or is open to a committed GPU hybrid.
 - If committed model: can procurement sign a 12-month commit at a known reserved throughput (we'll need to nail expected steady-state tokens and peak concurrency).

I'll flag any items that materially change price (e.g., encryption modes requiring HSM-backed KMS, extra retention on logs) in the one-pager. Grace / Marissa — can you confirm whether we should include a capped overage mechanism in the initial SOW?

Thanks,
Rishi
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
